subject: Equality constraints specified using matrix operations?

messages.author: 84e6ff87e445f88b
messages.subject: Equality constraints specified using matrix operations?
parts:
Hello everyone,
I'm wondering if we can specify constraints by using matrix operations on coefficients. Brief simulation with arbitrary number and questions at the end, thank you!!
JB

library(lavaan)
library(stringr)


n=1e6
b1 = 0.1
b2 = 0.2
a1 =0.4
a2 = 0.5
c = 0.7
 
(population.model1 <-
    str_glue('                     #use library stringr to pass the estimates to the model
             #paths and loading
             Y ~ {b1}*X1 +{b2}*X2 + {c}*GF  
             X1 ~ {a1}*GF
             X2 ~ {a2}*GF

'))
myData1 <- simulateData(population.model1, model.type="lavaan",sample.nobs=n,return.type="data.frame",standardized=TRUE)

 ###Estimated models

modela <-'
Y ~ b1*X1 +b2*X2 + c*GF  
X1 ~ a1*GF
X2 ~ a2*GF
X1 ~~x12*X2
l := a1*b1 + a1*x12*b2 + a2*x12*b1 + a2*b2
m := a1*b1 + a2*b2
'
#note l and m same here but differ for other simulations
fit1a <- sem(modela, data=myData1,estimator="GLS")
parameterEstimates(fit1a,standardized=T)

What I need is to be able to impose constraints on m or l. I know I can do that directly, e.g. by adding m == 0.30
But I need to programme in a way that could take any number of X.
A compact way to write that is to have two vectors of coeffs  A=c(a1,a2,a3...) and B=c(b1,b2,b3) and to use a matrix specification m:= AT %*% B
and l := AT %*% R %*% B with R being matrix of cor between Xs.  
So, question 1 is: can we impose equality constraints with that sort of matrix notation in lavaan.
And 2, more generally, how can I write syntax for model a in a way that is easy to extend. For example, the end user would just specify the number of Xs and the proper model would be specified.
Any pointer greatly appreciated. I think this can be done in programmes like OpenMx using matrix specification but keen to remain in lavaan or simplicity.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints specified using matrix operations?
parts: I'm wondering if we can specify constraints by using matrix operations on coefficients
Have you tried to do it?

What I need is to be able to impose constraints on m or l. I know I can do that directly, e.g. by adding m == 0.30
But I need to programme in a way that could take any number of X.

What is X in this case?  X == 0.30, so m == X?

If neither m nor X are scalars, but matrices of equal dimension, do you want to constrain each m[row,col] to equal the corresponding X[row,col]?  You can set up the values (or labels) in a matrix outside your lavaan syntax, than write a loop that specifies each constraint in a string.  Check out this way of specifying a saturated model, in case it helps you get where you want to go:

varnames <- paste0("x", 1:6)
covstruc <- outer(varnames, varnames, function(x, y) paste(x, "~~", y))
satMod <- c(paste(varnames, "~ 1"), # mean structure
            covstruc[lower.tri(covstruc, diag = TRUE)]) # cov structure
cat(satMod, sep = "\n")

library(lavaan)
fit <- lavaan(satMod, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit)

A compact way to write that is to have two vectors of coeffs  A=c(a1,a2,a3...) and B=c(b1,b2,b3) and to use a matrix specification m:= AT %*% B
and l := AT %*% R %*% B with R being matrix of cor between Xs.

I'm not really sure you are talking about specifying equality constraints or user-defined parameters.  You can use the matrix() function to do either, but you will not be able to define a user-defined parameter that is a matrix (user-defined parameters must be scalars).  If you try, you will get warnings and notice that the user-defined parameter will only be the first value [1,1] in the matrix you tried to define.
So, question 1 is: can we impose equality constraints with that sort of matrix notation in lavaan.

As long as the matrix operation results in a scalar, then it should work fine.  Once again, you can use paste() and c() cleverly enough to assemble a character vector of lavaan model syntax that does what you need, while automating the definitions you need.
And 2, more generally, how can I write syntax for model a in a way that is easy to extend. For example, the end user would just specify the number of Xs and the proper model would be specified.

Here is an example I threw together to try answering your questions.  A little Rchaeology goes a long way, so don't be afraid to simply try things yourself to see what happens.

mod <- ' visual =~ L1*x1 + L2*x2 + L3*x3
    x1 ~ T1*1
    x2 ~ T2*1
    x3 ~ T3*1
    arbitrary1 := t(matrix(rep(1, 3))) %*% matrix(c(L1, L2, L3))
    same_as_1  := sum(L1, L2, L3)
    arbitrary2 := t(matrix(rep(1, 3))) %*% matrix(c(T1, T2, T3))
    same_as_2  := sum(T1, T2, T3)
'
fx.con <- ' arbitrary1 == 3
arbitrary2 == 0
visual ~~ NA*visual
visual ~ NA*1
'
summary(cfa(mod, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv = TRUE))
summary(cfa(c(mod, fx.con), data = HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv = TRUE))
I think this can be done in programmes like OpenMx using matrix specification but keen to remain in lavaan or simplicity.

But this doesn't sound simple ;-)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Hi Terrence,
Thank you, that is so useful!!! I was able to do what I wanted (posted below).
I did not know outer() function. Is there any tutorial/link that lists  similar functions that perform this kind of operations on string of characters.
For example, the first thing I tried was to specify what I wanted outside the lavaan model but, not suprisingly, did not work as matrix operation did not work with characters.
So sth like:
given:
matrixA=matrix(c("a11","a21","a12","a22"),2,2)
matrixB=matrix(c("b11","b21","b12","b22"),2,2)
Is there a function that perform the equivalent of
matrixA %*% matrixB
where the cell in the first row first column of resulting matrix would be the character string: "a11*b11 + a21*b21"
Thank you again!
JB

n=1e6
b1 = 0.1
b2 = 0.2

a1 =0.4
a2 = 0.5

(population.model1 <-

             #paths and loading

'))
myData1 <- simulateData(population.model1, model.type="lavaan",sample.nobs=n,return.type="data.frame",standardized=TRUE)

head(myData1)

#estimated model
NX=3
namesX=paste0("X",1:NX)
covstruc <- outer(namesX, namesX, function(x, y) paste(x, "~~", y))
labelsa=paste0("a",1:NX)
labelsb=paste0("b",1:NX)

modela= c(
  paste("Y","~",paste0(paste0(labelsb,"*",namesX),collapse="+")),
  paste(namesX,"~",paste0(labelsa,"*","G")),
  covstruc[lower.tri(covstruc, diag = TRUE)],
  paste0("m1:=",paste(paste0(labelsa,"*",labelsb),collapse = "+")),
  paste0("sameas_m1:=","t(matrix(","c(",paste0(labelsa,collapse=","),")))","%*%","matrix(","c(",paste0(labelsb,collapse=","),"))")
 
)

const <- 'm1 ==0.40'

fit1a <- sem(modela, data=myData1,estimator="GLS")
parameterEstimates(fit1a,standardized=T)

fit1a <- sem(c(modela,const), data=myData1,estimator="GLS")
parameterEstimates(fit1a,standardized=T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints specified using matrix operations?
parts: I did not know outer() function. Is there any tutorial/link that lists similar functions that perform this kind of operations on string of characters.

Not that I am aware of; you just pick up R tricks over the years.  The function is typically used to calculate an outer product of two vectors (i.e., the resulting matrix is the product of all combinations among the 2 vectors).  The FUN= argument simply allows a different operation to be performed on all combinations between 2 vectors.  More general combinations can be manipulated similarly using the combn() function (e.g., for every combination of 3 values out of a set of 5 values, do some function).

matrixA=matrix(c("a11","a21","a12","a22"),2,2)
matrixB=matrix(c("b11","b21","b12","b22"),2,2)
Is there a function that perform the equivalent of
matrixA %*% matrixB
where the cell in the first row first column of resulting matrix would be the character string: "a11*b11 + a21*b21"

No, there is not a similar generalization of an inner product (and that "math" doesn't look like an inner product, unless b21 should be b12, so you "multiply" the first column of A with the second row of B).  But you could cross the number of columns in A by number of rows in B using expand.grid().  Then write a 2-argument function to do what you want for each ColA--RowB combination (and a third argument to name the user-defined parameter created by each combination?).  Finally, use mapply() to apply that function to each row of the expand.grid() output.

matrixA=matrix(c("a11","a21","a12","a22"),2,2)
matrixB=matrix(c("b11","b21","b12","b22"),2,2)

RCs <- expand.grid(ColA = 1:ncol(matrixA), RowB = 1:nrow(matrixB))
## name user-defined parameters?
RCs$parName <- paste0("A", RCs$ColA, "B", RCs$RowB) # or customize them
## define function to write indirect effects
makeParams <- function(CA, RB, PN = NULL) {
    vecA <- matrixA[ , CA]
    vecB <- matrixB[RB, ]
    products <- paste(vecA, vecB, sep = "*")
    if (is.null(PN)) return(paste(products, collapse = " + "))
    # else
    paste(PN, ":=", paste(products, collapse = " + "))
}
## apply to each row of RCs
RCs$definition <- mapply(makeParams, CA = RCs$ColA,
                         RB = RCs$RowB, PN = RCs$parName)
RCs

Then you can paste whichever defined parameter(s) you want into a script.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Thank you!!! Did a slightly different version that produces the matrix resulting from matrixA %*% matrixB but with labels in each cell corresponding to matrix multiplication. But yours allows to paste specific parameters in script which is great!
matrixA=matrix(c("a11","a21","a31","a12","a22","a32"),3,2)
matrixB=matrix(c("b11","b21","b12","b22"),2,2)

RCs <- expand.grid(RowA = 1:nrow(matrixA), ColB = 1:ncol(matrixB))
## define function to write products for each cell
makeParams <- function(RA, CB) {
  vecA <- matrixA[ RA,  ]
  vecB <- matrixB[,CB ]
 return(products <- paste(vecA, vecB, sep = "*",collapse = " + "))
 }
## apply to each row of RCs  and create resulting matrix
MatLabels <- matrix(t(mapply(makeParams, RA = RCs$RowA,
                         CB = RCs$ColB)),nrow=nrow(matrixA),ncol=ncol(matrixB))
